title: Which 20 formulas do you need for case interview maths?
description: The twenty formulas case maths keeps using, explained in plain English: profit, margin, break-even, growth, payback and more.
hook: You do not need much maths for case interviews, but you do need a small set of formulas so well that you never hesitate. Here are the twenty that come up again and again, in plain English.
body:
TermFormulaWorth knowing
ProfitRevenue − CostsRevenue = volume × price; costs = fixed + variable
Profit marginProfit ÷ RevenueMargin is always on revenue
MarkupProfit ÷ CostMarkup is on cost. Don't mix it up with margin
Contribution marginPrice − Variable cost per unitDrives all breakeven maths
Breakeven volumeFixed costs ÷ Contribution margin per unit'How many units to justify it?'
PaybackInvestment ÷ Annual net cash gain (extra profit or saving)Compare with the client's time frame
ROIAnnual profit ÷ InvestmentA yearly rate: compare with the hurdle rate or cost of capital
EBITDARevenue − COGS − Operating costs (excl. depreciation & amortisation)Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation & amortisation; the base for valuation multiples
Expected valueΣ (outcome × probability)Launch and bid decisions
PerpetuityCash flow ÷ r (growing: CF ÷ (r − g))Value today of a steady stream; for the growing version, CF is next year's cash flow
NPV ruleInvest if NPV > 0i.e. return > cost of capital
CAGR(End ÷ Start)^(1/years) − 1Rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ growth %
Market shareOur sales ÷ Market salesSay whether it is units or value
Elasticity% change in volume ÷ % change in priceState the volume assumption behind any price move
UtilisationActual output ÷ Maximum outputCheck before adding capacity
LTVProfit per customer per year × Years retainedSimple, undiscounted version. Compare with CAC; LTV:CAC of 3+ is a common rule of thumb
CACSales & marketing spend ÷ New customersRule of thumb for subscription businesses: earn it back within about 12-18 months
ChurnCustomers lost ÷ Customers at startRetention = 1 − churn; avg lifetime ≈ 1 ÷ churn
Cost-to-revenueEach cost line ÷ Revenue, over timeFinds the cost that is ballooning
Net working capitalInventory + Receivables − PayablesA cash trap in growth cases

How to learn them

Cover the middle column and say each formula out loud. Do it once a day for a week and they will stay. When you use one in a case, say the formula before the numbers so the interviewer can follow.
outro: The same list, with a test-yourself mode, is on the free formulas page. Next in this topic: Can you solve these 13 case interview maths questions in your head?
